judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line instruction that the persons insured provisions 'are changed to read as follows'; nothing ambiguous in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the HPL Persons Insured list (c043), but later endorsements (c091/c197 adding (g), c183 medical staff, c037 rotating physicians) amend the same provision again, so the operative roster is layered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare heading and lead-in; there is nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It introduces the substituted list and is consistent with the endorsement's instruction in c051.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three words identifying the named insured as an insured; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Named insured' is expanded well beyond Item 1 by Form 009-052 (c092) and Endorsement 13 (c211), so the class this paragraph covers is set elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional partnership/joint venture clause, clearly drafted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The named insured is designated a corporation in the declarations, so this paragraph is inert rather than conflicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Manager, supervisor' are broad, undefined job descriptors and the qualifier 'while acting within the scope of his duties as such' is fact-dependent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps but does not conflict with the employee paragraph (c056) and the medical staff extension (c183), which cover administrative capacity separately.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exception is hard to parse: it is unclear whether 'who is permanently practicing in Wisconsin' qualifies both physicians and nurse anesthetists, and the proviso on injury to employees with its professional-services carve-back is convoluted.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes licensed physicians while Endorsement 1 (c037) covers rotating unlicensed physicians and the medical staff endorsement (c183) covers staff physicians in administrative roles, and c091/c197 add a paragraph (g) that cross-refers to 'Section (d)' of a different form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Formal accreditation or similar professional board or committee' uses a general trailer after a specific example, but the class is narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates in substance the HPL medical-incident limb (b) (c046) and the CGL professional-board paragraph (c062(g)) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Coverage turns on the undefined boundary of 'administrative duties' as opposed to clinical practice, a line that is genuinely contestable for a Medical Director or Chief of Service.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Medical Staff extension (c183/c185) draws the same administrative/professional-services line for overlapping persons and makes that coverage excess (c186), so two provisions cover the same individuals on different terms.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite limitation on undesignated partnerships and joint ventures.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is repeated in the CGL persons insured provisions (c063, c131) consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As respects the coverage provided by this endorsement' limits the disapplication of Exclusion (c), but the endorsement is a persons-insured provision rather than a coverage grant, which blurs the reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (c) (c041) is also disapplied by the Medical Staff endorsement (c184) for a different set of persons, so the exclusion's surviving scope depends on reconciling both.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line amendment instruction; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the CGL Persons Insured provision (c131), which nonetheless remains printed in the coverage part, and the Broad Form adds further insureds (c161).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The lettering is defective — the list runs (a)–(e) then jumps to (g) with an unlabelled paragraph in between — and 'any person or organization for whom the named insured is, by written agreement prior to loss, obligated to provide such insurance' is an open-ended class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supersedes the printed CGL Persons Insured provision (c131) while the Broad Form Additional Persons Insured (c161) adds employees again with restrictions this list does not contain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definite limitation identical in substance to c059.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the corresponding sentence in the printed CGL Persons Insured provision (c131) with no divergence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its inception-date default matches the endorsement's stated effective date of 03/01/1996.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only with respect to their interest in the operations of the Named Insured' is a vague limiting phrase, and the schedule's 'insurable interest' entries ('as their interest may appear') are indefinite and mis-aligned with the names.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement 6 (c073) adds insureds on a differently worded basis ('only as respects their contract'), and Form 009-052 (c092) makes some of the same entities full named insureds, e.g. Seeger Health Resources.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amendment adds a single word, 'Humiliation,' to a numbered item without saying how it operates, and the item referenced ((D)1) is 'false arrest, detention, imprisonment or malicious prosecution.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: In Form L6111 the Personal Injury definition item 1 is false arrest and the like (c142), so inserting humiliation there does not fit the provision it purports to amend.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence promising sixty days' notice 'in the event of cancellation or non-renewal' with no carve-out, so whether it covers cancellation for non-payment is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Condition 11's thirty days (c034) and the Cancellation–Wisconsin form's ten-day and forty-day periods (c107, c108, c109), and only partly matches the sixty-day non-renewal rules in c100/c111.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends a form by title, misciting it as 'Exclusion (cd),' and 'air ambulances' is added without saying whether ownership or use matters.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-050 (c188) already deems patient loading and unloading a health care service, so this further amendment overlaps it, and both operate on HPL exclusion (d) (c042).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Only as respects their contract with the Named Insured' is a compressed limitation whose scope (liability arising from the contract? performance under it?) is not spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses a different limiting formula from the Endorsement 2 additional insureds (c065), but the two schedules do not overlap in named entities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To and/or on behalf of the insured only' and 'a specific patient injury occurrence which could potentially result in a professional liability claim' are loose, and the $7,500 cap runs by calendar year.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cap is measured in calendar years while the policy period runs 03/01/1996–03/01/1997, and the exclusions that follow are said to apply to 'Coverage E' although this grant is not labelled Coverage E.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The Company will not provide for the defense of the insured' sits immediately beside a promise to reimburse defence costs, and the reimbursement is limited to proceedings 'instituted by the Medical Licensing Board' where the insured holds an active licence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (1) that follows (c077) excludes proceedings initiated by state licensing boards relating to health care delivery, which appears to withdraw the very coverage this paragraph grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The exclusion sweeps 'state licensing, regulatory or quasi-governmental boards or agencies, professional review organizations (PRO); or Medicare/Medicaid' — a broad list closing with an equally broad relational phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes precisely the Medical Licensing Board disciplinary proceedings that the grant in c076 promises to reimburse, an apparent direct contradiction within the same endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific exclusion of sanctions, penalties, fines and restitution; the terms are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes 'a covered proceeding,' which depends on the contested interaction of c076 and c077.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line exclusion of criminal proceedings; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits consistently with the other Coverage E exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Narrow and specific: payment, refund and admissions-approval proceedings before the licensing board.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps exclusion (1) (c077) but adds nothing inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Excluding 'any actions involving disputes with respect to this insurance' is broad and self-serving, but its target is identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the Overlap Endorsement (c175), which promises to indemnify the insured for expenses in determining which insurer bears a loss — a coverage this exclusion appears to cut against.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Alleging that the insured has conspired with another to institute ... an investigation' is oddly drafted, but its subject is identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses the same matter; it fits within the Coverage E exclusion list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Aware prior to the effective date ... which the insured could reasonably believe would result in such costs' is a known-loss test resting on a subjective/objective hybrid.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It parallels the Pollution endorsement's retroactive date mechanism (c177) but does not conflict with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'To any matter other than a disciplinary proceeding' is an absolute exclusion whose breadth is not qualified in any way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read literally it removes the legal-consultation and interview/deposition coverage granted in c075, which are not disciplinary proceedings at all.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow exclusion for medical staff applications; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the medical staff endorsement (c183) without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Disputes solely involving allegations of fraud, or wilful non-compliance' makes coverage turn on the undefined word 'solely.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates ground covered by exclusions (1) and (8) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deletes 'Exclusion (D) of Section II – Premises Medical payments Coverage,' but Premises Medical Payments is Section III of Form L6111, so the citation misidentifies the provision it destroys.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section II of L6111 is Personal Injury and Advertising Injury (c138–c142), whose item (D) is a definitions paragraph, while the medical-payments exclusion (D) is c147 — so which provision is 'null and void' is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attaching language; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the endorsement's own effective date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Charitable health care services in their communities' is an undefined class, and the deeming sentence conclusively characterises those acts as within the scope of employment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-137 WI (c196) restates this identical extension elsewhere in the same policy, and Additional Condition B (c050) says the policy does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident except as stated in the HPL Part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The added paragraph (g) defines the covered employee by reference to 'Section (0d) of this endorsement,' but this endorsement contains no section (d) — a broken cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical paragraph is added a second time by Form 009-137 WI (c197), and the intended referent is paragraph (d) of Form 009-109 WI (c056), which the text does not say.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of named insureds with a single qualifier; the entities are identified, though 'no automatic coverage for entities newly acquired by any of them' is compressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Broad Form Automatic Coverage provision (c163) grants 90-day automatic named-insured status to newly acquired organisations, which this endorsement purports to withhold, and Endorsement 13 (c211) adds a further entity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite deeming rule about notice of cancellation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the cancellation provisions (c034, c106–c111) but must be read alongside the sixty-day endorsement (c069), which speaks only of 'the insured.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional preamble ('when this policy is issued or delivered in the State of Wisconsin'); definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The policy is issued by an Ohio company to a Wisconsin insured, so the condition is satisfied and the endorsement's amendments compete with the parallel Form 009-095 WIS amendments (c114–c117).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as reasonably possible' and 'specific circumstances involving a particular person likely to result in a claim' are elastic notice standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Condition 4(a) (c023), which the HPL coverage part has already replaced with a differently worded Condition 4 (c048), leaving two competing amended notice duties for the same coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph is numbered '4.' though it is the second item in a list running 1., 4., 3. — a numbering error — and its second half reverses the first half's rule about agents.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-095 WIS (c116) makes the same amendment in slightly different words (omitting 'prior to loss'), and both contradict the printed Changes condition (c031).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text contains a plain duplication error — 'affects the company's obligation under this policy breach of a promissory warranty affects the company's obligation unless...' — which garbles the promissory-warranty rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-095 WIS (c117) states the same paragraph cleanly, so the instrument contains two versions of one rule, one of them corrupted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence, 'Moreover, the Action Against Company Condition does not apply,' appended without explanation or qualification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-095 WIS (c114) deletes that same condition and replaces it with an operative substitute, so one endorsement abolishes what the other re-enacts — an unreconciled conflict with c026 as well.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed four-ground list for cancellation; 'substantial change in the risk assumed' and 'substantial breaches' are evaluative but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Cancellation–Wisconsin form (c109) lists three of the same grounds with a ten-day notice period, while this endorsement supplies no period, and Endorsement 4 (c069) requires sixty days.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear statement that the company need not renew, with detailed machinery for longer-than-annual policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Cancellation–Wisconsin form (c111) gives the named insured an affirmative 'right to renewal' on similar terms unless sixty days' notice is given, which pulls directly against 'the company shall not be obligated to renew.'
